plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flowers (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. Grows outdoors as a large shrub in warm climates and is widely used as a potted holiday plant elsewhere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide in warm regions and as an indoor plant
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants, so they need long uninterrupted nights to develop their colorful bracts. The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used the sap for medicine and the bracts for dye.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like flowers. Early-flowering cultivars open in the cool months of winter, brightening gardens when little else blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens in the southeastern United States, Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan, the camellia (tsubaki) has long been associated with winter and the tea ceremony.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like leaves that becomes covered in brilliant clusters of flowers. Southern Hemisphere populations and some tropical regions bloom around the summer months, making it a spectacular sight at Christmas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February in the Southern Hemisphere); late spring to summer in the tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, South America, the Caribbean and Africa
plants.funFact: Although it is a famously common tree in the tropics, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar. Its long seed pods can reach 60 cm and rattle in the wind.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens. It flowers in the depths of winter, often pushing through frost and snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to mountainous woodlands of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and northern Apennines; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true rose and is entirely unrelated to the rose family; it belongs to the buttercup family. All parts of the plant are toxic, and legend says it first bloomed from the tears of a girl with no gift for the Christ child.
